## Motivation

To support CPU core management in CBB mode for next Gen Xeon. This is a re-submit of #36850 , accommodates the recent changes in #40066 .

## Modifications

Expand core topology query function parse_lscpu_topology to query both NUMA and CBB (via L3 cache affinity). Then auto detect the core management mode base on the parsing results. Other utilization methods are updated accordingly.

## Tests

Core binding functionality is validated on a next (7th) Gen Xeon.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

-    Usually we can get the SNC information (How many available) from the Operating System with e.g. `lscpu` command.

nodes.body: **[blocking]** Splitting on `[,:]+` drops empty CSV fields. For example, with the `CPU,Core,Socket,Node,,L1d,L1i,L2,L3` layout, `1,1,0,,,1,1,1,0` is parsed as `[1, 1, 0, 1, 0]`: the L1d cache ID becomes the NUMA-node ID instead of preserving the previous empty-node fallback to 0, producing incorrect binding groups and memory budgets. Please preserve the first four CSV columns, parse cache fields separately, and add a raw-output parser regression test; the current topology test mocks out this parser.

@@ -186,12 +186,13 @@ Notes:
 
 2. The flag `--tp 6` specifies that tensor parallelism will be applied using 6 ranks (TP6).
     The number of TP specified is how many TP ranks will be used during the execution.
-    On a CPU platform, a TP rank means a sub-NUMA cluster (SNC).
-    Usually we can get the SNC information (How many available) from the Operating System with e.g. `lscpu` command.
+    By default, each rank is bound to a group of physical CPU cores.
+    SGLang reads `lscpu -p=CPU,Core,Socket,Node,Cache` and groups cores by Compute Building Block (CBB), identified by L3 cache ID, when there are more L3 cache IDs than NUMA nodes. Otherwise, it groups cores by NUMA node, including sub-NUMA clusters (SNCs) exposed as NUMA nodes.
+    Each group is restricted to the process's allowed CPU affinity, and empty groups are excluded from rank assignment.
 
-    If the specified TP rank number differs from the total SNC count,
-    the system will automatically utilize the first `n` SNCs.
-    Note that `n` cannot exceed the total SNC number, doing so will result in an error.
+    Ranks use the first available groups in NUMA node or L3 cache ID order.
+    Without an explicit binding, the total rank count (`dp_size * tp_size * pp_size`) cannot exceed the available group count.
+    A CBB is a CPU binding group, not a separate NUMA memory node; multiple CBB groups can share one NUMA node.
 
     `SGLANG_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND` allows explicit control of CPU cores for each tensor parallel (TP) rank.

For example, with the `CPU,Core,Socket,Node,,L1d,L1i,L2,L3` layout, `1,1,0,,,1,1,1,0` is parsed as `[1, 1, 0, 1, 0]`: the L1d cache ID becomes the NUMA-node ID instead of preserving the previous empty-node fallback to 0, producing incorrect binding groups and memory budgets. Please preserve the first four CSV columns, parse cache fields separately, and add a raw-output parser regression test; the current topology test mocks out this parser.

+    Without an explicit binding, the total rank count (`dp_size * tp_size * pp_size`) cannot exceed the available group count.
+    A CBB is a CPU binding group, not a separate NUMA memory node; multiple CBB groups can share one NUMA node.
 
     `SGLANG_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND` allows explicit control of CPU cores for each tensor parallel (TP) rank.
